steps.text: This chart shows every Nobel Prize in physics, chemistry, medicine and economics from 1901 to 2023, arranged by the year it was awarded.
Each dot is one prize winner. This is Jennifer Doudna, who shared the 2020 prize in chemistry for developing CRISPR gene editing.

The height of each dot shows how well-off the winner's father was, based on his occupation, compared with everyone else in the same country. A dot at 90 means his job paid more than 90% of jobs in that country. More than 65% of laureates grew up in households in the top 10%.
When we take country income into account, laureates are even more elite, because there are very few laureates from poor countries.
